impacts.description: Accelerated deployment and adoption of AI agent solutions in industry through the European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) network.
Stronger R&I capacity and output among participating organisations and better transfer of knowledge between participating organisations.
Strengthened European AI research and development community through sharing of communicable results on the AI-on-demand platform.

impacts.inference_note: The call states 'regular feedback of research results into teaching and education at participating organisations' as an expected outcome; the impact framing — sustained knowledge circulation between research and education — is inferred as the systemic effect of that feedback loop, beyond the immediate organisational outcome.

impacts.description: New mind-sets and approaches to R&I work fostered through international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience, enriching the broader European research culture.
impacts.source_section: Expected Outcome — For supported postdoctoral fellows
impacts.inference_note: The call states 'new mind-sets and approaches to R&I work forged through international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience' as an expected outcome for fellows; the impact on the broader European research culture is inferred as the systemic effect of many fellows bringing these new approaches back into host organisations and the research community.
impacts.description: AI agent innovation in healthcare, advanced manufacturing, and in-vehicle autonomous driving sectors, addressing sector-specific real-world application challenges.
impacts.inference_note: The portfolio coverage exception (procedure_exceptions in HORIZON-CL4-2026-05-DIGITAL-EMERGING-02.json) mandates that grants cover at least one proposal in each of three sectors: healthcare, advanced manufacturing, and in-vehicle autonomous driving. This requirement is logically derivable as an impact priority signal: the EC would not impose a sector portfolio guarantee unless these sectors were recognised impact domains for this topic. The scope text also frames AI agents as holding 'significant promise in numerous applications areas', reinforcing the inference that sector-level economic and societal impact is an intended outcome of the topic.

impacts.description: Enhanced European strategic autonomy in AI through integration with AI Factories, Data Labs, and Testing and Experiment Facilities.
impacts.inference_note: The scope text explicitly requires projects to link to AI Factories and Data Labs and states results may be validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities (call_entry.scope). The topic destination heading is 'Achieving open strategic autonomy in digital and emerging enabling technologies'. The mandatory institutional linkage to these European AI infrastructure elements logically implies that strengthening European technological autonomy in AI is an intended impact; projects would not be required to link to these infrastructure elements unless their use contributed to this strategic objective.
